recipes.name: Decadent Peanut Butter Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed and divided
1 (11.75 ounce) jar Smucker's® Hot Fudge Microwaveable Ice Cream Topping, divided

steps.text: Beat together 1 cup peanut butter, cream cheese and sugar in a medium bowl with an electric mixer on medium, until well combined. Gently mix in 3 cups whipped topping until thoroughly combined. Spoon mixture into pie shell. Using a spatula, smooth mixture to edges of pie.

Reserve 2 tablespoons of hot fudge topping into the corner of a resealable plastic bag. Microwave remaining topping, on HIGH (100% topping), for 1 minute. Stir. Spread topping over pie, covering entire peanut butter layer. Refrigerate until set. Spread remaining whipped topping (1 1/2 cups), over hot fudge layer, being careful not to mix the two layers.

Cut a small corner from bag containing topping. Squeeze bag to drizzle topping over pie. Place remaining 2 tablespoons peanut butter in a resealable food storage bag; cut bag corner and squeeze to drizzle in opposite direction from topping. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Decadent Peanut Butter Pie
raw_recipe.description: The famously irresistible duo -- peanut butter and chocolate -- come together in this rich and creamy pie.

review.reviewBody: This pie deserves more than five stars. My boyfriend and I found the recipe on a coupon or something at the store last summer and immediately bought all the ingredients and made it that night. It is the best! We make it several times per year. We always used to order peanut butter pie for dessert at restaurants, but don't do it anymore because this recipe is just so much better, not to mention cheaper. I like to use Neufchatel cheese and drizzle the pie crust with the fudge first. French Vanilla Cool Whip is a yummy substitution as well. Edited 5/26/10 to add: we've made this many times over the past few years. My fiance actually proposed to me while we ate this pie together! I know it's just a fluffy recipe with convenience food ingredients, but it will always be special to us.

Full disclosure, I can't review the recipe as written because I made a few small changes. I'm not wild about frozen whipped topping so I whipped my own heavy whipping cream instead. I also made a ganache by melting semi sweet chips with cream instead of using jarred hot fudge, and crushed a pack of Oreos with 1/3 cup butter for the crust. That said, this recipe comes together in no time and is just really fantastic. Sadly, there is never a piece left over for me to have with my coffee the next day...

Loved the cake, made it for my boyfriend as a celebration for the end of summer classes. The peanut butter filling is wonderful and the cake is just rich enough for it not to be too heavy, but really really yummy! I piped the whipped topping instead of smearing it, dusted with cocoa powder and drizzled the melted fudge with a spoon instead of a bag. I also added some chopped up Reese’s and it was delicious! Exactly what I wanted in a chocolate/peanut butter pie!

I made a sugar free version. To make up for missing "real sugar, I made homemade whip cream, I found it made the dessert so rich folks didn't realize I had used splenda instead of sugar. I also took the murrays sugar free chocolate cookies and made a crust from scratch, along with smuckers sugar free hot fudge. Friends are always asking me to make it, I don't tell them it's sugar free until after they taste it. Even though cool whip makes a sugar free whip topping take the extra steps of making it from scratch, this is the key, without it, you won't get the same reviews.

Love the pie but I obviously didn't know what I know now after making it! I used reddi-whip but it wasn't frozen like cool whip and so top was runny.. I let the filling set for about 2 hours which I should have let it set overnight in the refrigerator before putting the whip topping on over the fudge layer. I ended up scraping the melted layer of whip topping into a separate dish. I added cool whip and then topped with the drizzle of hot fudge and peanut butter also adding crushed peanuts, Reese peanut butter chips, and peanut butter cookies next and finished with mini Reese peanut butter cups! I made one with oreo crust and one with graham cracker crust. I froze one and refrigerated one and both came out very decadent even though it was not as beautiful as the original picture. Tasted fabulous!

Oddly I found this same recipe in a Skippy ad. Only difference is it uses 1/3 c sugar, not 1/2. It is the best peanut butter pie I've tried yet, so go for the less amount of sugar. I'm a Jif fan but have always been told Skippy makes better fudge. I have to say, it also makes better pie. I am now expected to make this pie for every picnic and party. When all done I put peanut butter in a baggie and hot fudge in another baggie, melted 10 seconds in the microwave, then cut a tiny piece of the corner off and drizzled all over the pie. Beautiful! You could also chunk up Reece's cups for the top.

Very dense and intensely peanut-buttery! It is definitely for die hard peanut butter fans, like me! I would recommend beating the cream cheese and peanut butter mixture for longer, to get some air in and to create a lighter texture. Pie was a bit denser than what I'd imagined. I used 1 cup icing sugar in place of the regular white sugar. I figured it would lend a smoother texture. Also used 1.5 cups of whipped cream (whip the cream, then measure 1.5 cups) instead of whipped topping, I prefer real whipped cream. I made my own chocolate syrup for the topping, that recipe is also from allrecipes :)

My whole family loves this recipe! It's the perfect peanut butter pie. I didn't have hot fudge so I used Nutella instead. Also just used a regular pie crust. Delicious! I spread some Nutella on the crust after it cooled than put on the peanut butter topping. Added some streaks of Nutella on the top too. So yummy

Made this over the weekend with a few minor changes just because I didn't want to make another trip to the grocery store! The recipe calls for 2 Tbsp. of peanut butter to be added to the cream cheese and sugar for the filling but I used a whole cup. I beat the pb, cream cheese and sugar in my stand mixer until it was all incorporated and then added all of the cool whip and beat it on high until it was fluffy like mousse!! I also melted a whole bag of milk chocolate chips and spread a thin layer on the crust, added the filling and spread the remainder of the melted chocolate on top and stuck it in the fridge. THIS PIE IS AWESOME!!

This pie is delicious and rich. I add a little more peanut butter and a sprinkle of powdered sugar because my family is peanut butter crazy. I omit the hot fudge layer, make homemade whipped cream, and sprinkle with cut up miniature Reese’s cups after swirling melted chocolate chips and warmed peanut butter. So good!
I have made this for Thanksgiving for the last two years. I skip the chocolate, add coarsely chopped peanut butter cups on the bottom and top, and use fresh whipped cream. Delicious!
Quick easy and so delicious.
My husband's favorite pie. I make it just for him. He may share! Haha

This is our family’s absolute favorite dessert. It deserves at least 10 stars. Sometimes I use a graham cracker crust and drizzle a bit of the chocolate topping on the bottom. I have a daughter that needs gluten free so I either make a separate small crustless one or I’ve also crumbed up gluten free animal crackers or gf graham crackers for her crust.

This has become my favorite dessert ! I now double it and make in a 9x13. I crush up 'oreos' for the bottom layer, and I usually top it with chopped up reese's cups ! Oh my, now I'm going to have make one today just thinking about it. It's truly decadent 5+++ stars for me.
I’ve made this twice, once with homemade pie crust with graham crackers an the other with the chocolate crust... my kids loved both and I’m making it now the 3rd time!!

I wasn’t sure about this pie, having never had peanut butter pie before. Although, it is a southern favorite and my husband, being from the south, loves anything chocolate and peanut butter so I thought I would give it a try. Oh my God! It is so good! It’s surprisingly light and not too sweet although that could be because I made homemade whipped cream instead of Cool Whip. It’s only because I hate Cool Whip. Also, the only suggestion I would give is to make it in a springform pan instead of using a ready-made gram cracker crust in a pie pan. Simply just easier to cut and easier to work with when assembling. Otherwise, I am going to make it again!

This is literally the best recipe and the most popular item I’ve brought to any party! I add crushed Oreos on top. I also split this recipe into two pies so consider buying two pie crusts if you’re going to make it!

I have made this several times and my family loves it. My 9 year old grandson requested this instead of a birthday cake. It seems to me if you use the store bought chocolate pie tin it will make 2 just add a little extra peanut butter. It has become the most requested dessert in my family!
I've made this several times for family gatherings and it is always very popular. I follow the recipe as written, no tweaks needed.
